### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7041c60bca4c1609c8eed634c6e11bab0684d2ff` — the merge of head `60b4b97f37ffe387a4e93b681b2bcabe7c3d7304` into base `1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7041c60bca4c1609c8eed634c6e11bab0684d2ff && git checkout 7041c60bca4c1609c8eed634c6e11bab0684d2ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 60b4b97f37ffe387a4e93b681b2bcabe7c3d7304 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 && git merge --no-ff 60b4b97f37ffe387a4e93b681b2bcabe7c3d7304

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `60b4b97f37ffe387a4e93b681b2bcabe7c3d7304`
Local-runs: none

PR #22641 on card #22578, segment 4 of the maintainer's ruling A on #22438 (director record `6079645593`, split request `6092059305`). Inputs, and nothing else: the card body and its four comments (unlock scan `6094525572`, claim `6094944537`, os-dev-report `6095296313`, claim amendment `6095306881`); the PR body and its six-file list; the net diff `git diff origin/main...60b4b97f37` (+504/-1); and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. ADR-0043 and the member's docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` were read at the head as the governing text; the locked `hono@4.13.12` was read for its parser semantics.

**Check-runs on the head:** 35 check names, latest run per name, all completed: 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, which runs only when the pin moves, and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, 0 in progress; the last to finish was `Lint & Repo Gates` at 2026-10-10T08:22Z. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts for every derived family: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Validate Package Dependencies, Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check lanes, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core (six shards and the gate), Dogfood (three shards, the gate and Verify CLI), Temporal Conformance, and the card, branch and single-writer guards. No verdict was rendered while any of them was still in progress.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A new public member on the published class — right.** `ApprovalService.handleActionPage(request: Request)`, returning a Promise of a `Response`, matches the optional contract member's signature exactly; the class already declares `implements IApprovalService`, so the implementation is checked by the type-check lanes, which are green. No other export changes: `ACTION_PAGE_PATH` and `actionPageResponse` are module-private.
2. **GET accept-set — right.** The token is read from the `token` query parameter (first occurrence, as `URLSearchParams.get` and Hono's `query()` both read it), `peekActionToken` is the one check, a live token answers the confirm page and a dead one the result page, both `200` with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, and nothing is decided. This is the contract's GET and the mount's GET.
3. **POST accept-set, repeated field read as its last value — right.** The mount reads `parseBody()` then `body.token`; in the locked Hono, `parseFormData` assigns `form[key] = value` per entry in order unless `all` is set, so a repeated key resolves to its last value. The member reads `formData().getAll('token')` and takes the last, so the two doors agree on every body. A non-form body is `{}` at the mount and a thrown `formData()` at the member, both an empty token and the "invalid" page. `redeemActionToken` is the one redemption chain. The parity pin measures all of this byte for byte on one token store, including the repeated field whose live first value stays live at both doors.
4. **Methods other than GET and POST answer `405` with `Allow: GET, POST` — right.** The contract and ADR-0043 name only GET and POST, and the contract says the one caller forwards only those two, so no third method reaches the member from its caller; for a resource that exists but does not support the method, `405` with `Allow` is the correct HTTP answer and narrower than inventing GET semantics for a third verb. The mount itself answers a stray method with Hono's not-found and serves HEAD as a bodiless GET at the app level; neither is a contract behaviour, and neither is a parity case. HEAD is carried to #22576 (see ③).
5. **Same token checks, no second credential — right.** The diff adds no token lookup, no page text, no copied chain, and no read of `request.headers`, a context, a session or a cookie; the member imports the two renderers the mount already imports. The pin-4 header spy can only observe JavaScript-side reads, so this judgment rests on the diff, which shows none.
6. **Byte-unchanged mount, no double mount — right.** The pre-image of `approvals-plugin.ts` in the diff is `main`'s blob (`51fd00eb78`), and the only hunk is one inserted statement before the existing early return; both route handlers are untouched, the member is not mounted, and the composition pin reads exactly `GET` and `POST` on the path.
7. **The one added log line — ordered by the card, honest only once #22576 lands.** It says the pages "are served through the HTTP dispatcher's /approvals/act domain". On `origin/main` `1b99388505` the dispatcher has no approvals domain, so between this landing and #22576's a kernel with no raw app logs a route that still answers `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. The card's own text prescribes this line, the dev declared the window in the PR body and the report, the line is `info`-level and carries no tracker number, and the fix is landing order rather than a change to this diff. Judged right as ordered; escalated in ③.
8. **`actionLinkUrl` — no surface change.** The constant extraction emits the same bytes.
9. **Test and package surface — right.** The test boots inside each case, imports only this package's sources and its devDependencies, reads nothing outside the package, and is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program that the package's `typecheck` script names through `check:test-typecheck`; all four Type Check lanes are green. Nothing under `dist/`, `exports` or `files` changes.
10. **Nothing governed, nothing out of lane.** None of the six paths is a governed surface (Governed Surface Queue Guard green); `packages/spec`, `packages/runtime`, `plugin-hono-server` and `content/docs/releases/` are untouched, as the claim required.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes

`.changeset/22578-approvals-action-page-member.md` declares `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: minor` and carries `Clause-②: yes`, as the PR body does. The diff publishes one additive public member on a published class, which is `yes` and at least `minor`; it removes or renames nothing, so no arm and no ADR-0087 marker is owed; `skip-changeset` would be wrong. `Check Changeset` is green. The `hono` devDependency publishes nothing: devDependencies are not installed by consumers, and `dist/`, `exports` and `files` are unchanged. One observation, not a ground: the lockfile row records `specifier: ^4.13.5` under a manifest that says `^4.13.9`; the three sibling importers on `main` (`adapters/hono`, `plugin-auth`, `plugin-hono-server`) carry the identical pair, and CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` under the pinned pnpm is green on this head and on `main`, so the row matches its siblings rather than its own manifest and the install accepts it. A repo-wide lockfile refresh, if wanted, is its own card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag 1 — file surface grew by `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` (claim amendment `6095306881`).** Answered: test-only, unpublished, and the parity pin genuinely needs a real Hono raw app; see ② for the lockfile observation.
- **Dev flag 2 — the log line names a domain that lands with #22576.** Answered in ① item 7. Escalated to the owning seat: sequence #22576 so the window stays short, and if a release is cut while it is open, the release board should carry one line saying a dispatcher-only kernel logs that route before the runtime of the same release serves it.
- **`open_questions`: none declared, none found.**
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 1 (HEAD) — correctly carried by #22576, and must actually reach it.** Hono serves HEAD as a bodiless GET at the app level on the mount; the member answers `405`. Whether a HEAD is forwarded to the member as a GET, forwarded as HEAD, or refused in front is the dispatcher domain's decision and must be written in #22576's acceptance, not inferred; no outcome decides anything, so it is not a safety question. The dev wrote "noted, not filed", which leaves the finding in a report on #22578 that #22576's dev will not read: the seat should relay both findings onto #22576 in one comment before that card is dispatched.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 2 (log line) — same carrier.** #22576's acceptance 3 (a typed refusal, never `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`) is what closes it; the relay above covers it.
- **The NOT MEASURED leg — right to report, and owed by #22576.** The card's third pin ("with the member absent, segment 2's typed refusal answers") cannot be measured until the dispatcher domain exists; on `origin/main` `1b99388505` the dispatcher names no approvals domain, which I read directly. Reporting NOT MEASURED instead of faking the leg is the rule. Escalated: #22576's acceptance must carry that ablation explicitly, and since `ApprovalService` now always has the member, that ablation has to remove it (or the `approvals` slot) on purpose; #22438 stays open until it is measured.
- **Docs drift check.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` was named through the `ApprovalService` symbol only; it carries no action-page text, so nothing there contradicts the change and no edit is owed. The release page it names is read-only by rule.

Reviewed-by: `session_013j5gkUCpqQiti4GgPqqmnt` (contract-review subagent, CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)

**VERDICT: PASS**
